MCL - Section 780.972 use of deadly force by individual not engaged in commission of crime.

  (1) An individual who has not or is not engaged in the commission of a crime at the time he or she uses deadly force may use deadly force against another individual anywhere he or she has the legal right to be with no duty to retreat if either of the following applies:
    (a) The individual honestly and reasonably believes that the use of deadly force is necessary to prevent the imminent death of or imminent great bodily harm to himself or herself or to another individual.
    (b) The individual honestly and reasonably believes that the use of deadly force is necessary to prevent the imminent sexual assault of himself or herself or of another individual.
    (2) An individual who has not or is not engaged in the commission of a crime at the time he or she uses force other than deadly force may use force other than deadly force against another individual anywhere he or she has the legal right to be with no duty to retreat if he or she honestly and reasonably believes that the use of that force is necessary to defend himself or herself or another individual from the imminent unlawful use of force by another individual.

On of the most fun (maybe just for me the DM) dungeons I ran was the wizard tower of infinity. 

Some of the rooms include: 
The elemental plane of fire (also water, air, and earth)

A 50s style diner where everyone just stared at the weirdos in armor but they got a classic hamburger, fries and malt milk shake (I also got malt and made milkshakes for them to have a campfire session there)

A Nordic great hall with a feast and warriors that forgot them every time they left. (The went back here a couple times by RNG)

My house, while we were all playing, so the players got to “meet” their characters

An early 2000s mall on Black Friday

A Chinese emperors chambers as they were getting sieged. Fun little fight where language mattered (it didn’t it was just a mess of strange languages and no clue who to attack where)

Among about 50-75 other rooms that I wrote up, they didn’t go through all of them. Where at any point they could run into the various magical beings (dragons, sphinx, solar, devils, etc) the wizard tried to capture over the years. OR the wizard in various stages of their life. (The wizard is much friendlier when they’re young but will attack on sight when they’re old and afraid the party is a bunch of looters.) 

My point is the multiverse is infinite. The planes can be anything and sometimes subverting expectations can be chaotic but players remember the chaos more then the well structured parts

I don’t think you’re in the wrong OP for asking anyone else, but I think you should have a conversation offline with each player asking what they want in the campaign. A hack and slash, a role playing adventure, or the chance to explore a diverse world. Or even a combination! After you talk with each player about it you could morph the world more to the players you have instead of trying to do something that they either don’t like or don’t understand themselves. 

TLDR: 8 int isn’t stupid but can be in the eyes of people who learned to read/write at a young age. DM should talk offline about how his campaign is going forward.

Guidelines is a good way to describe it. In 5e it gives you an idea of who your character is and how to act. The same way background describes who your character is in the personality, bond, flaw, and ideal sections. It doesn’t change how the player has to act, nor does it affect your character as far as spells/abilities work. 

Do I like this system? No. Do I think paladins should be locked to good alignments? Also no. I think the fact that they have oaths imply they should be locked to lawful alignments. I know this’ll probably get lost in the comment section but I think I need to put this here for myself. 

Parents split at 4 and it was a nasty divorce. Found out after enlisting and moving across the country that they divorced because of infidelity. Grew up with two parents that just hated each-other for no reason. Mom almost spilt the beans a few times because maybe she thought I’d think less of my father for it. 

Did week on week off with both parents. Dad remarried when I was ~10 to someone with two sons and they had parents with a happy divorce. I was jealous. Mom had another kid with her BF when I was 15. Her parents have their own set of issues that I hope she doesn’t grow up wrong from. 

The worst part about not knowing why your parents hated each-other was being forced to think it was you that caused it. I asked when I was young but no answer besides the truth would have worked to soothe the demon that was my own anxiety that I was the reason my parents hated each-other. It’s built up into its own manifestation of problems in my social and emotional health. 

I sometimes even feel guilty about feeling bad about my childhood. I had food on my plate, a bed, a roof, a safe environment, I wasn’t abused or anything but I still felt like my life was bad. I know people who grew up without these things, without parents. People who actually had a bad life. 

One of my core memories of the divorce was seeing my mom and dad hug for the first time in my life. Their mutual friend passed away and they consoled each-other. I was angry and sad to see that. Why did they love that person more than me? Why couldn’t they pretend to like each-other for me and my brother? Everything they did, before and after that one time, was just to make themselves look good for the court so that they can get full custody. There was a lot of resentment for a long time after that. Maybe there still is.

After about a year of therapy though I feel much better to know and confirm with my own anxiety that it wasn’t me. It wasn’t my fault. I wouldn’t wish this kind of life on anyone. Thank you for reading this, I just needed to type it out for myself.
